title: review: F6: a merge that comes back tests_red holds the task for the Planner instead of leaving it failed with merged_at stamped
spec:
Gotcha 2026-09-19 18:22 (T-0241): orchestrator/daemon.py merge_reviewed (about line 640) stamps pipeline.merged_at before calling merge.merge so a conflict is attempted once; when merge.merge returns status tests_red (worktree gate green, review approved, suite red only in the rebased merge run, here a flaky thread test) merge.merge sets the task failed reason tests_red, report_merge only notifies, merged_at stays stamped, and nothing retries or asks the Planner. The Planner had to notice by hand.
Change daemon.py:
1. In merge_reviewed, after report_merge: when the returned status is not "merged", set the task status held with hold_reason "merge <status>" (for example "merge tests_red", "merge conflict") and keep reason/resume_hint from merge.merge; clear pipeline.merged_at only for tests_red so a later fix round or Planner re-approval can retry the merge exactly once more; conflicts keep merged_at (today's once-only rule). Use stamp()/bus.update under the bus lock as the surrounding code does.
2. held tasks with hold_reason starting "merge " must appear as decision points for planner_runs.decision_points() the same way review holds do (check planner_runs.py; if held tasks are already picked up generically, add a test proving it and change nothing there).
3. notify() text unchanged apart from the hold.
Tests in tests/test_daemon.py: test_merge_tests_red_holds_task (merge.merge monkeypatched to return {"status": "tests_red", ...}: task ends held, hold_reason "merge tests_red", merged_at cleared), test_merge_conflict_holds_and_keeps_merged_at, test_merge_ok_unchanged. Keep every existing test green; the suite now runs spawn_async synchronously in tests (T-0245).
acceptance: a held task with hold_reason starting 'merge ' is yielded by planner_runs.decision_points() (existing behaviour proven by a test, or added)
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
